label: Taiwan
description: Global hub for leading-edge foundry (TSMC) and OSAT (ASE). Concentration of advanced logic and CoWoS packaging makes Taiwan the central chokepoint in the chain.

label: United States
description: Home to fabless giants (NVIDIA, AMD, Apple, Qualcomm), wafer-fab equipment (Applied Materials, Lam, KLA), and CHIPS Act fabs — but still dependent on Taiwan/Korea for leading-edge volume.

label: South Korea
description: Dominates DRAM, NAND, and HBM (Samsung, SK hynix). Korea is the memory counterpart to Taiwan's logic concentration — a second Asian single point of failure.

label: China
description: Hosts foreign memory/OSAT/foundry assets and pushes domestic champions (SMIC, YMTC, CXMT). Export controls cap leading-edge tool access; mature-node capacity is expanding fast.

label: Japan
description: Quiet dominance in photoresist, specialty chemicals, and Tokyo Electron coat/develop tools. A materials or toolchain shock here slows every advanced fab worldwide.

label: Netherlands
description: ASML's EUV lithography monopoly makes the Netherlands the strategic gatekeeper of the leading edge — central to US/EU export-control policy toward China.

label: Singapore
description: Mature-node foundry (UMC) and packaging/test hub in Southeast Asia. Regional staging point between Taiwan/Korea fabs and global customers.

label: Germany
description: GlobalFoundries Dresden and European auto/industrial chip demand. EU industrial policy and automotive supply depend on trailing-edge capacity here.

label: Ireland
description: Major Intel fab and European fabless back-office hub. Part of the US/EU manufacturing footprint outside Asia.

label: Israel
description: Intel leading-edge R&D and fab campus; strong fabless design ecosystem. Key US-allied manufacturing node in the Middle East.

label: Malaysia
description: Backend assembly, test, and packaging for memory and logic. Lower-cost Southeast Asian node in the downstream chain.

label: India
description: Growing assembly, design, and packaging footprint as firms diversify out of China. Micron and others expanding memory-related capacity.

label: Canada
description: Design and research presence for US-linked chip firms. Not a major fab geography but part of the North American talent pool.

label: Costa Rica
description: Intel mature-node assembly and test. Illustrative of nearshore Americas capacity for trailing-edge work.

label: Poland
description: Intel back-end and European supply-chain diversification. Part of EU efforts to spread manufacturing beyond Germany.

label: Vietnam
description: Fast-growing EMS and assembly alternative to China (Samsung, Intel, and Apple suppliers). Downstream systems layer shifting south.

label: Mexico
description: Nearshore EMS and systems assembly for North America. Foxconn and others expanding as firms de-risk China-only assembly.

label: Philippines
description: OSAT and packaging operations (Amkor and others). Southeast Asian packaging node supporting US and Taiwan customers.
